# No Padding, No Problem

Checking the instance we get the following:

```
└─$ nc wily-courier.picoctf.net 57489  
Welcome to the Padding Oracle Challenge
This oracle will take anything you give it and decrypt using RSA. It will not accept the ciphertext with the secret message... Good Luck!


n: 
e: 65537
ciphertext: 
```

Every time you connect you will get a different n so leave the connection open if possible.

You can create a cipher using the `encrypter.py` and then use `cipher_to_string.py` to get the original string.

```
Give me ciphertext to decrypt: 
Here you go: 
```

We spent a bunch of time going down the wrong rabbit hole.  The solution is to use this formula:

```
E(m) * t^e mod n = (m * t)^e mod n = E(m * t)
```

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleability_(cryptography)

The above E(m) is encrypted message we want to crack, t is a random message we are adding, e and n are from RSA.

Use the `mixed_encrypter.py` script to create an encrypted message.  Send that message to the oracle and get back a decrypted long number `mt`.

The problem is the `mt` is both messages so we need to remove our message from it using this formula:

```
m = mt * t^-1 mod n
```

This is found in the `mixed_cipher_to_string.py` file.  Bob's your uncle.  Actually, this was very hard for me and Omar.  It took us 2 hours to solve with the Internet and some clanker help for the Python formulas.  You can see our struggles at:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Xm0E2Ut70j0
